get.summary: List addresses

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 1,000 (default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: at_least
parameters.description: Read at least this store revision (read-your-writes after a write).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only addresses with one of these statuses: `planned`, `active`, `reserved` or `deprecated`. Repeat the parameter or separate the values with commas.

parameters.name: vrf
parameters.description: Only addresses of this VRF (identifier).

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: Only addresses inside this network, for example `192.0.2.0/24`. A bare address is a host network. Host bits must be zero.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Only addresses whose most specific prefix is this prefix (identifier).

parameters.name: interface
parameters.description: Only addresses assigned to this interface (identifier).

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Only addresses assigned to an interface of this host (identifier).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only addresses that carry every one of these tags. Repeat the parameter or separate the tags with commas.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text search over the address, the DNS name, the description and the tags.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: comma-separated fields, `-` in front for descending, for example `-updated,ip`. Fields: `ip` (the default), `dns_name`, `status`, `created`, `updated`.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Deleted addresses: `exclude` (the default), `include` or `only` (the restore view).

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `host`: each address bound to an interface also carries `interface_detail` (`id`, `name`, `mac`, `duid`) and `host` (`id`, `name`, `mode`, `lock`), read from the same view as the page. Both are absent for an unbound address, when the interface or host is deleted, and when the principal may not read interfaces and hosts. Does not change the cursor.

200.description: A page of addresses

get.summary: List audit records
get.description: Newest first unless `order=asc`. Filters combine with AND. `principal` is a subject such as `user:<uuid>`, `token:<uuid>` or `system:api`; `action` is exact or, when it ends with a dot, a namespace prefix such as `ipam.prefix.`; `object` is a kind such as `prefix`, or `kind:uuid`. Records are read in sequence order and a request examines at most 20,000 of them: when that runs out first, the page holds the matches found so far, possibly none, and `next_cursor` continues the scan. `next_cursor` is null only when the scan reached the end of the log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 1,000 (default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: at_least
parameters.description: Read at least this store revision (read-your-writes).

parameters.name: principal
parameters.description: Principal subject, for example `user:<uuid>`, `token:<uuid>` or `system:api`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
Audit action, exact (`ipam.prefix.create`) or a namespace prefix ending with a dot
(`ipam.` or `ipam.prefix.`).

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: Object reference `kind:<uuid>`, or a bare kind such as `prefix`.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Outcome: `success`, `denied` or `failed`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Records at or after this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Records before this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc`.

200.description: A page of audit records

403.description: Not allowed

get.summary: Verify the hash chain of the audit log
get.description: Walks the whole chain from record 1 and reports the first record that does not verify: a gap in the sequence, a record that does not link to its predecessor, or one whose hash no longer matches its content. `checked` counts the records that did verify, `head` is the last of them and `store_head` the newest record of the log. Reads the whole log; on a long log it takes a while.

200.description: The verification report; `intact` is false when the chain is broken

403.description: Not allowed

parameters.description: Sequence number of the audit record, from 1
